title: SPHEREx 0.75-5 um spectrophotometry shows a 3.1 um water-ice absorption band and a hot-dust excess in the old dipper star Gaia20cdd during its 2025 low state
abstract: Gaia20cdd is a kinematically old K-type star with deep dips that prior campaign work attributed to small dust grains; it also has a 4.6 um excess. No spectrum of the star exists (we found none in DESI DR1, LAMOST DR10-12 or SDSS DR19). We made forced PSF photometry with Gaia DR3 positions on 441 SPHEREx Quick Release 2 images of Gaia20cdd (2025 June to 2026 July) and on 2,300 images of eight other campaign dimmers, with more than 400 field stars as controls. ZTF shows that Gaia20cdd was in a shallow low state (g 0.30-0.35 mag, r 0.15 mag) in the two SPHEREx windows with optical data, before and after a 2.9-mag dip. In both windows (2025 July 19 and December 18), the flux at 2.98-3.17 um is 0.33 +- 0.05 below the local continuum (9.3 sigma in a per-star test); no other measured star shows a band above 3 sigma. Simultaneous 0.86-0.94 um exposures show no extra dimming, the band falls on different detector pixels, and five PSF and aperture variants keep it. The band matches the 3.08 um peak of water ice. A Mie model with small ice grains (radius about 0.1 um) plus silicate fits the 0.47-3.4 um extinction (chi2 85.8 for 169 points; silicate alone 110.7); the water column is about 6e17 molecules per cm2. SPHEREx also confirms the 4.6 um excess (0.20 mag, redder than 97-98 percent of 187 control dwarfs of similar colour), with no excess at 3.1-3.75 um and a blackbody temperature of 940 K (750-1260 K) from SPHEREx alone, or 610 K with the WISE 12 um point. The M dwarf Gaia DR3 3768075658908734720 also has an excess; the deep dimmer Gaia DR3 2870538750879109504 has no excess, no band and no NEOWISE W1 change in its 2018-2020 low state. Thus in 2025 an ice-rich cloud of small grains crossed an old star that also has persistent hot inner dust, which agrees with icy comet-like material. Limitations: the band rests on four exposures in two visits; SPHEREx QR2 calibration is preliminary; we used crystalline-ice constants and simple screen models; other 3 um absorbers are not excluded; no high-resolution spectrum. display.caption: SPHEREx spectrophotometry of Gaia20cdd in 2025-26. Top: binned flux density and the photosphere template from 12 same-field control K dwarfs. Bottom: single-exposure ratios target / controls (normalised at 2.0-2.35 um) by window, with the best ice-plus-silicate Mie model (solid) and the best silicate-only model (dotted). The 3.1 um absorption band and the hot-dust excess above 3.5 um are visible.

Tests of the 3.1 um band. (a) Band-depth signal-to-noise ratio for all measured stars in nine fields; only Gaia20cdd exceeds 3. (b) Target / control ratios in the two SPHEREx sequences that cover the band: detector 4 at 2.86-3.15 um (filled) and the same-time detector-1 exposures at 0.86-0.94 um (open).

(a) SPHEREx [3.1-3.75] - [4.3-4.95] um colour against Gaia BP-RP for 344 control dwarfs (grey) and the nine dimmers; Gaia20cdd and Gaia DR3 3768075658908734720 (G3768) are redder than the control locus; G2698 was in a faint state. (b) ZTF depth of Gaia20cdd below its quiet level in 2024-2026 with the three SPHEREx windows.
